long_biography.plain_text:
Harris Group became a leading Irish commercial-vehicle distributor by building its platform around imported marques and long supplier relationships. Robert “Pino” Harris secured Hino after encountering the Japanese maker at an overseas motor show, then added Isuzu, Iveco, Kia and other brands. By the mid-1990s, the group’s three main truck franchises held a quarter of Ireland’s heavy-goods-vehicle market.

Harris brought a practical formation to the business. Raised in a Dublin family whose father worked in scrap metal, he had little formal education but developed strong mechanical and sales skills. He stayed close to workshops and customers even as he diversified into property and other investments. When Harris died in 2017, his wife Denise took responsibility for a group built on distribution, service and technical credibility.

The date is retained as research evidence, but the three death-date fields are not proposed because the frozen Alive status caused inventory to classify them as inapplicable; only mortality is corrected in this pass.
